description: The pie chart represents the distribution of difficulty levels in a dataset. There are five slices corresponding to the categories: Medium, Hard, Easy, Very Hard, and Very Easy. The Medium category is the largest, comprising 51.8% of the dataset, followed by the Hard category at 25.7%. The Easy category accounts for 11.2%, the Very Hard category is 6.5%, and the Very Easy category is the smallest at 4.7%. Each slice is color-coded and labeled with both the category name and the percentage it represents. The chart includes a legend in the upper left corner, which matches the colors to the difficulty categories. The slices are not ordered by size, and there are no additional visual emphases such as exploded or offset slices. The chart is titled "Distribution of Difficulty" and is designed to provide a clear visual representation of the proportion of data entries across different difficulty levels.
